objections.eyebrow: The objection we hear every call
objections.p1: We hear this on almost every first call.
objections.p2: Here is the belief behind it.
objections.item2: Agencies are a middleman cutting into the developer's salary, so the developer isn't motivated.
objections.item3: Freelancers are a legal and financial risk.
objections.item4: Agency developers aren't in it for the long run, they job-hop.
objections.reframe1: The developer on that 4 year engagement didn't job-hop.
objections.reframe2: He became the person the client's own team leaned on.
objections.reframe3: That's what happens when the margin is fair and disclosed, not padded and hidden, and when the match is right from day one instead of rushed to fill a seat.

protocol.title: How the Quick Staffing Protocol works.
protocol.scopeText: You tell us the role, the stack, the niche requirement. We don't send you a questionnaire, we get on a call and get it exact.
protocol.matchText: We pull from developers already vetted for niche roles in your industry, not a cold search that starts after you sign.
protocol.placementText: You get a developer matched to your stack, ready to start. Billed hourly, at the salary rate plus our €10/h margin. No surprise invoices.
protocol.retentionText: If the fit works, the developer stays embedded in your team for as long as the project needs. The 4 year engagement is the proof this isn't a revolving door.
protocol.ctaLabel: Start the protocol with a free call

proof.title: One developer. One enterprise automotive project. Four years.
proof.p1: One of our developers spent 4 years embedded on a single enterprise automotive project.
proof.p2: He built the front-end from zero. Sole front-end developer on the team.
proof.p3: Delivered on time, in budget, at Senior standard. Zero quality issues.
proof.p4: He adapted through a Kanban to Scrum transition and an on-premise to cloud migration.
proof.p5: He mentored junior developers on his own initiative. Nobody asked him to.
proof.p6: The project lead told us he wants to bring him back through RSA SOFT for future projects.
proof.closing1: That's the standard we place developers to.
proof.closing2: The Protocol is how fast we do it.
proof.videoCaption: Hear it directly from a client RSA SOFT has delivered for.

faq.title: What else you should know before you call.
faq.q1: How fast is a developer actually ready to start?
faq.a1: Usually 24 to 48 hours after the scope call: we draw from developers already vetted for your industry instead of starting the search after the contract is signed.
faq.q2: How does billing work, and what does it really cost?
faq.a2: Hourly, at the developer's rate plus a flat 10 €/hour margin. You see both numbers. Nothing extra is baked in, whether the search takes 48 hours or 4 weeks.
faq.a3: The difference is transparency: you see the developer's rate and our margin separately instead of one marked-up flat fee. No middleman skimming off the developer's pay without you seeing it.
faq.q4: What's the legal basis for the engagement?
faq.a4: Every custom software development engagement is governed by a separate written agreement signed before the project starts.
faq.q5: Does the developer only stick around for the first sprint, or longer-term?
faq.a5: As long as your project needs them. The reference case in our proof section ran 4 years on the same team.
